page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL40S is an accelerated compute instance combining shared central processing resources with dedicated graphics hardware. The system is provisioned with 8 vCPUs sourced from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Physical core allocation matches the vCPU count with one thread per core. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB of system RAM, allocating 8.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 48 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent file systems, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core execution speed alongside specialized inference capabilities. The AMD EPYC core achieves top-tier scores in single-core stress-ng (4184.99) and Geekbench single-core evaluation (2903.0), supported by comprehensive vector extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16. Multi-threaded metrics fall in the median tier due to the 8-core boundary, with multi-core stress-ng reaching 33593.88 and PassMark CPU scoring 28778.84. Memory performance tests strong, recording 178.06 GB/sec on large block uncached reads and a PassMark memory score of 2959.37.

Machine learning inference benchmarks highlight strong performance on compact to mid-sized language models powered by the L40S accelerator. Generation throughput reaches 448.64 tokens per second on 135M parameter models and 33.46 tokens per second on 7B models. Throughput diminishes significantly when processing large 70B parameter models, yielding 3.19 tokens per second for generation and 6.59 tokens per second for prompt ingestion due to the single-GPU memory footprint.

The qualitative cost profile favors mid-scale accelerated workloads that do not demand expansive multi-GPU arrays. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff requiring external network storage configurations. The instance is suited for AI inference, lightweight model fine-tuning, computer vision processing, and accelerated rendering pipelines.

The hardware does not include bundled local storage, necessitating external storage volumes for data persistence. Benchmark analysis demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU throughput and solid memory bandwidth, while multi-core compute remains within median ranges. The dedicated accelerator provides strong throughput for small and medium language model inference, such as 33.46 tokens per second on 7B models, but encounters scaling constraints on 70B parameters. With 8.0 GB of RAM per core alongside specialized vector instructions including AVX-512 BF16, this server fits machine learning inference, computer vision, visual rendering, and graphics-accelerated engineering pipelines.
